info.title: Thrivea Public API
info.description:
Thrivea's public REST API: a customer's own systems read and write their Thrivea data.

### Basics
| | |
|---|---|
| **Base path** | `/v1` |
| **Media type** | `application/json` |
| **Auth** | `Authorization: Bearer <API key>` |

### Authentication
An API key is created in Thrivea and carries the scopes it was granted. Send it as a bearer token on
every call. A key acts within its own workspace only.

### Lists and pagination
A list is `{ "object": "list", "data": [...], "has_more": true|false, "url": "..." }`. Page with
`limit` and the id of the last item you hold in `starting_after` (or the first in `ending_before`).

### Errors
A failed call answers with an HTTP status and `{ "error": { "type": "...", "message": "...", "param": "...", "request_id": "..." } }`.
`type` is the stable value to branch on: `invalid_request_error` (400), `authentication_error` (401),
`permission_error` (403), `resource_missing` (404), `conflict_error` (409), `rate_limit_error` (429),
`api_error` (5xx). `message` is for people and logs.

### Request ids
Every answer carries a `Request-Id` header, and every error body the same value as `request_id`. Quote it
to Thrivea support and we find the call in our logs.

### Idempotency
A `POST`, `PATCH` or `PUT` may carry an `Idempotency-Key` header (1 to 255 characters of your choosing).
The first 2xx answer to a key is kept for 24 hours and replayed to a retry with the same key, with
`Idempotent-Replayed: true`, so a client that timed out and retried never creates twice. The same key with a
different request is a 400; the same key while the first request is still running is a 409. The key is
scoped to your API key.

### Rate limits
Requests are counted per API key in a fixed window. Every answer says where you stand: `RateLimit-Limit`,
`RateLimit-Remaining`, `RateLimit-Reset` (seconds until the window ends) and `RateLimit-Policy`
(`600;w=60`). Over the limit the answer is 429 `rate_limit_error` with `Retry-After`; wait that long.

post.summary: Submit an application, as JSON (no CV).
post.description:
The same path also accepts multipart/form-data with these fields in snake_case (tags repeated or
comma-separated) and the CV in an optional file field named cv.
The candidate is found by email or created; an existing candidate keeps the name Thrivea holds. A first
application to the job answers 201. The same candidate applying to the same job again, the next day or a
year later, updates that one application and answers 200: a new CV becomes the current version and the
earlier ones stay, a new cover note replaces the old, a new phone number goes onto the candidate, and an
application that was rejected or declined goes back to the first stage. One rejected permanently, or ended in a
hire, keeps its stage, and its new CV and cover note are kept without telling anyone. Otherwise the hiring team
is told of a new CV, a new cover note or a reopened application, never of a retry. The tags are added to the
candidate either way; external_ref stays the one sent first.

Scope: `write:candidate_applications`.

object.description: String representing the object's type. Value is "list".

has_more.description: True if there are more candidates after this page.

Candidate.description:
A candidate, as the system that sent the application needs them back: who they are and the tags they carry. No
applications, comments, CV or pipeline position; those stay with the hiring team.

object.description: String representing the object's type. Value is "candidate".

first_name.description: The candidate's first name, as given on their first application.

last_name.description: The candidate's last name, as given on their first application.

email.description: The e-mail the candidate is known by; one candidate per e-mail in a workspace.

headline.description: A one-line headline, when a recruiter wrote one.

tags.description: The candidate's tags by name, e.g. #frontend-engineer.

created_at.description: Time at which the candidate was created.

updated_at.description: Time at which the candidate or their tags last changed; the creation time until then.

CandidateApplication.description: An application a candidate made to one job opening.

object.description: String representing the object's type. Value is "candidate_application".

candidate_id.description: The candidate, reused when the e-mail is already known.

external_ref.description: Your id for the submission, as sent.

has_cv.description: Whether a CV was stored with the application.

cv_version.description:
The number of the current CV among the CVs the application has had, starting at 1; absent with no CV. A candidate
who applies again with a new CV moves it up by one, and the earlier CVs stay with the application.

updated.description:
On a 200, whether this request changed the application that already existed: a new CV, a new cover note, or
a closed application reopened. false on a 201, on a retry, and on a request whose only news is a phone
number, which goes onto the candidate rather than the application.

created_at.description: Time at which the application was made.

CandidateApplicationBody.description:
The body of POST /v1/candidate_applications, as JSON or as the fields of a multipart/form-data request
that also carries the CV in a file field named cv. In a form, tags repeats or is comma-separated.

job_opening_id.description: Required: an open job opening, job_….

first_name.description: Required. Used when the candidate is new; an existing candidate, found by email, keeps the name Thrivea holds.

last_name.description: Required. Used when the candidate is new; an existing candidate keeps the name Thrivea holds.

email.description:
Required. The candidate with this e-mail is reused. A second application to the same job is the first one, answered
with 200: a new CV becomes its current CV (the old one is kept), a new cover note and phone replace the old,
and an application that was rejected, though not permanently, goes back to the first stage and the hiring team
hears of it again. The same request sent twice changes nothing the second time.

phone.description: Optional. A number given here replaces the one the candidate had; an empty one keeps it.

cover_note.description: What the candidate wrote, and any form answers with no field of their own.

tags.description: Tag names, e.g. #frontend-engineer: found by name, created when missing, added to the candidate's own.

external_ref.description: Your id for the submission. Stored on the application.

object.description: String representing the object's type. Value is "list".

data.description: The cost centers on this page.

has_more.description: True if there are more cost centers after this page.

CostCenter.description: A cost center: a code that job positions are charged to.

object.description: String representing the object's type. Value is "cost_center".

id.description: Unique identifier for the cost center, e.g. cc_01h2xcejqtf2nbrexx3vqjhp41.

code.description: The cost center's code, at most 20 characters.

job_position_ids.description: The job positions charged to this cost center.

active.description: Whether the cost center is in use.

created_at.description: Time at which the cost center was created.

updated_at.description: Time at which the cost center last changed; equal to created_at until it does.

code.description: The cost center's code, at most 20 characters.

job_position_ids.description: The job positions charged to it.

UpdateCostCenterRequest.description: The body of PATCH /v1/cost_centers/{id}. A field left out keeps its value.

job_position_ids.description: The whole list of job positions charged to it; it replaces the list it had.

PeopleCriteriaResource.description:
Who manages, or who belongs to, an org unit: a rule, not a list. The people matched by any
rule in Includes, minus the people matched by any rule in Excludes.

includes.description: The rules a person must match one of to be in the group.

excludes.description: The rules that take a person out of the group even when an include matches.

PeopleCriterionResource.description:
One rule. Type names it (the snake_case tokens in OrgUnitCriteria) and the one field
that rule takes carries its argument; the fields the rule does not take are left out of the JSON. Ids are the
prefixed ids the rest of /v1 uses where a prefix is registered for the kind.

type.description: The rule: one of everyone, none, by_employee_ids, is_in_org_unit, is_org_unit_manager, has_job_position, works_at_same_site, is_in_permission_group, has_permission, has_erb_scalar_field, reports_to, is_direct_manager, is_indirect_manager, is_self, is_buddy, is_hrbp or is_it_admin. The field the rule needs is set beside it; treat a type you do not know as one added later.

org_unit_id.description: is_in_org_unit: the members of that unit.

job_position_id.description: has_job_position: the people in that job position.

site_id.description: works_at_same_site: the people at that site.

permission_group_id.description: is_in_permission_group: the members of that permission group. No prefix is registered for groups, so a plain GUID.

permission_name.description: has_permission: the people who hold that permission, by its stored name.

erb_field_id.description: has_erb_scalar_field: the people with a value in that employee record field. No prefix is registered for fields, so a plain GUID.

url.description: The https address events are posted to. Its host must resolve to public addresses only, checked again before every delivery.

description.description: What the endpoint is for, for your own records.

event_types.description: Required, one or more types from GET /v1/webhook_endpoints/event_types. An unknown type is a 400; an employee.* type asked for by an integration key is a 403.

enabled.description: Whether to send events to it. Read as true when left out.
